overview: Same genus, very different behavior — especially when it comes to which antifungal will actually work.
genZNote: Same genus, but one shrugs off azoles way more often.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: The most common cause of candidiasis, forming true hyphae/pseudohyphae and a positive germ tube test.
aspects.valueB: A non-albicans Candida species that grows only as yeast cells, with no true hyphae or germ tube formation.

aspects.label: Morphology
aspects.valueA: Yeast cells, pseudohyphae, and true hyphae depending on conditions.
aspects.valueB: Small, uniform yeast cells only — no hyphal forms.

aspects.label: Azole Susceptibility
aspects.valueA: Generally susceptible to fluconazole and other azoles.
aspects.valueB: Frequently exhibits reduced susceptibility or resistance to fluconazole, an important treatment consideration.

aspects.label: Clinical Relevance
aspects.valueA: Most common cause of oral thrush, vaginal candidiasis, and invasive candidiasis overall.
aspects.valueB: Increasingly common cause of invasive candidiasis, especially in older or immunocompromised patients and after azole exposure.

aspects.label: Identification on Chromogenic Media
aspects.valueA: Produces a distinct green colony color on many chromogenic Candida agars.
aspects.valueB: Produces a distinct pink to purple colony color on the same chromogenic media.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: A germ-tube-negative Candida from a sick, previously azole-treated patient should raise suspicion for C. glabrata.
